newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK ECONMIN CALLS FOR SELF-RESTRAINT IN RATE CUTS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK ECONMIN CALLS FOR SELF-RESTRAINT IN RATE CUTS.

text.p: Greece's National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou called on commercial banks to self-restrain themselves from cutting their deposit rates aggressively.
"Interest rate reductions should be in tandem with inflation," said Papandoniou. "Interest rate cuts should not outpace the deceleration of inflation."
CPI-inflation fell to 6.0 percent year-on-year from 6.6 percent in February.
"The Greek economy suffers from excessive confidence," said Papandoniou referring to the aggressive interest rate stance of some credit institutions.
Banks are correct in discounting future favourable developments but self-restraint should be applied, he added.
The rate of growth of tax revenues increased in March, said Papandoniou.
"I will have the final figures next week," he added.
The current account deficit was about 3.5 percent of GDP in 1996, in line with Greece's EU convergence programme, and would be close to $4.6 billion at year-end, Papandoniou added.

Central bank figures put the current account deficit at $4.75 billion in the first 11 months of 1996 compared to $3.023 in the same period of 1995. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
